children: Oil prices fall after President Trump said his administration reached an agreement for Russia to supply large amounts of diesel to the U.S. and global markets. Brent crude is down 0.6% to $104.90 a barrel, while WTI futures fall 0.8% to $91.10 a barrel. However, a more meaningful decline in refined product prices will require normalized conditions in the Middle East, according to ING. "Not just in the amount of oil flowing from the Persian Gulf, but also in the way this oil is coming out," analysts at the firm say. "Inefficient trade flows of oil from the Middle East have led to a significant surge in tanker freight rates, which will likely keep product prices elevated." Meanwhile, the geopolitical risk premium remains elevated following the deadly Houthi missile attack on Saudi Arabia's international airport on Saturday. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
